A. NH4Cl (Ammonium chloride): This is formed from the reaction of a weak base (NH3) and a strong acid (HCl). When dissolved in water, the NH4+ ion can donate a proton, creating an acidic solution. The reaction is:
NH4+ + H2O ⇌ NH3 + H3O+

B. Na2CO3 (Sodium carbonate): This is formed from a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (H2CO3). It produces a basic solution when dissolved in water, as the CO3²- ion can accept protons from water:
CO3²- + H2O ⇌ HCO3- + OH-

C. NaH2PO4 (Sodium dihydrogen phosphate): This salt contains replaceable hydrogen atoms. When dissolved in water, it can release H+ ions:
H2PO4- ⇌ HPO4²- + H+
This makes it an acidic salt.

D. Zn(OH)Cl (Zinc hydroxide chloride): This is a basic salt because it contains the hydroxide ion (OH-), which makes the solution basic.

Based on this analysis, NaH2PO4 is an acidic salt because it contains hydrogen atoms that can dissociate in water to produce H+ ions, making the solution acidic.
